claims: The Ivy League consists of eight private, highly selective research universities in the Northeastern U.S.

The Ivy League institutions are Brown University, Columbia University, Cornell University, Dartmouth College, Harvard University, University of Pennsylvania, Princeton University, and Yale University.
Brown University is located in Providence, RI.
Columbia University is located in New York, NY.
Cornell University is located in Ithaca, NY.
Dartmouth College is located in Hanover, NH.
Harvard University is located in Cambridge, MA.
University of Pennsylvania is located in Philadelphia, PA.
Princeton University is located in Princeton, NJ.
Yale University is located in New Haven, CT.
Brown University has an Open Curriculum.
Columbia University has a Core Curriculum.
Cornell University has colleges including engineering, agriculture, and hospitality.
Dartmouth College is the smallest Ivy League school.
Harvard University is the oldest institution in the U.S.
University of Pennsylvania is home to the Wharton School of Business.
The Ivy League originated as an NCAA Division 1 athletic conference in 1954.
Stanford, MIT, and Duke are not part of the Ivy League.
